findings.text: blocking: the roll folds the new contributions into the previous bucket's contributions but never removes the entries the new window's start has passed — _lane_rates_from (:273-277) only filters them out of the answer — so _LANE_RATE_BUCKETS retains every distinct row completed since the process's first read of that project, and each later bucket re-walks that whole retained set. That contradicts the comment at :164-165 ('The population a project's window can hold is the bound on memory'), the function's own docstring, the commit message's 'dropping the rows the new window no longer admits' and the fragment's 'drops the rows the section's new window's start has passed', and it makes a long-lived station's memory and per-bucket cost grow with process uptime rather than with the window, which is the exact bound the replaced lru_cache kept.

non-blocking: causes_first == base_causes_first (:247) and causes_next == base_causes_next (:279) compare the head code's warm path against the head code's cold path after cache_clear, not against the base revision's answers the done_when names, so despite the base_ prefix the two sides move together and any defect shared by both paths passes; the rates half is independent (ledger.load(PROJECT) recomputed at :163), and _budget_overrun_cause and _historical_reference_rate are untouched by the diff, so the gap is narrow rather than blind.
